goal.outcome: Determine whether direct native ICON interpolation of absolute W_SO is no worse than the legacy July 2 and 3 cold starts in slow-state compatibility and wind/PBL response.
goal.why_now: The direct-native SMI transform caused a persistent 39--42 kg m-2 retained-day soil-column bias, while the direct-native absolute-W_SO statics remove the 58--59 kg m-2 SMI wet shift and remain mean-neutral relative to the legacy statics.
goal.resource_rationale: Only the two established causal origins are rerun; two independent two-node trajectories fill a bounded four-node preemptible budget and use the validated shared-cache controller workflow.
evidence_needed: Retained-day soil water, soil temperature, and surface temperature bias against the unchanged continuous reference
Retained-day wind and PBL response against the unchanged continuous reference and legacy cold starts
Model-age evolution through 72 hours to test whether any direct-native absolute-W_SO perturbation decays
stop_conditions: Stop if either direct-native absolute-W_SO static initialization fails finite/range validation
Stop if the corrected production HICAR pin or frozen-wind regression contract is absent
Do not expand beyond the July 2 and 3 origins before the retained-day comparison is interpretable
